1.support: The aim of the present study was to determine whether an individualized titration of mechanical ventilation according to cardiopulmonary physiology reduces the mortality

2.support: Adult patients (≥18 years of age) with the following entry criteria were enrolled: (I) class III obesity (BMI > 40 kg/m2), (II) diagnosis of ARDS [4], (III) mechanical ventilation for > 48 h

3.support: The report states all patients meeting criteria were included but provides no denominator of screened or eligible patients from which a participation rate could be computed.
3.location: Page 4, Statistical analysis; no screening flow reported

4.support: During 2012–2014, mechanical ventilation settings of the first cohort of patients... was titrated according to ARDSnet PEEP/FiO2 guidelines. During 2015–2017... treated by the lung rescue team.
4.location: Page 2, Methods, Patients and measurements / Interventions

5.support: an a priori sample size calculation was not performed

6.support: During ICU admission and the first 4 days of mechanical ventilation, patient characteristics together with cardiopulmonary and hemodynamic were recorded. Patients' outcomes up to 1-year follow-up were also recorded.

7.support: Patients' outcomes up to 1-year follow-up were also recorded.
7.location: Page 2, Methods; Fig. 2 Kaplan-Meier to 365 days

12.location: Pages 2-5, Methods and Results (no blinding mentioned)

13.support: No deaths occurred in either group after 3 months, and the increased risk of mortality persisted in the standard protocol-based cohort at 6 months and at 1 year after admission.
13.location: Page 5, Results, Mortality; Fig. 2 shows complete 1-year follow-up

14.support: The Cox proportional hazard model was used to examine differences in survival after adjusting for predetermined potential confounders (BMI, age, APACHE, PaO2/FiO2 ratio).
14.location: Page 4, Statistical analysis; Table 3 footnote a

nih.rationale: Items driving the rating: No on item 4 (non-concurrent cohorts from different calendar years 2012-2014 vs 2015-2017, so secular trends in ARDS care confound the exposure-outcome relationship despite the authors' arguments), No on item 5 (no sample size or power justification), CD on item 3 (participation/screening not reported), and no blinding (item 12, NA). Strengths include clearly stated question (1), defined population and criteria (2), exposure preceding outcome (6), adequate timeframe and follow-up (7, 13), well-defined objective outcome (11), repeated physiological measurements (10), and adjustment for key confounders (14). Residual risk of confounding inherent to the retrospective before-after design prevents a Good rating, but objective mortality outcomes and multivariable adjustment keep it above Poor.
